operative_sections_inspected.quote: To: Mr. Colin Hartwell, Chief Executive Officer, Juvoxa Optics
Cc: [Name], Design Head, Juvoxa Optics; [Name], Relationship Manager, Juvoxa Optics

Juvoxa's lamp design has failed crash validation on our demo vehicles four consecutive times. After each failure ET and QT asked for a root-cause analysis, a corrective design and a dated recovery plan. We have not received a credible root cause, a committed plan or a named owner, and the design has not converged. Follow-ups and escalations have been met with little transparency and no decisive action.

Four failed validations, no corrective action and an unmet timeline are, in our view, a material breach of those obligations. [Purchasing to insert the relevant contract and clause references before sending.]
Model A's time-to-market has slipped by two months, which is about one-sixth of the first-year plan of 100,000 units pushed out.

1. Termination. Banyan Crest terminates Juvoxa's nomination for the Model A headlamp and will not consider Juvoxa for any future programme, with effect from the date of this email and subject to the termination provisions of the contract.

2. Refund. We formally request the return of 30% of the tooling and development costs paid upfront. On the quotation figures (tooling INR 10,000,000 and R&D INR 2,000,000, total INR 12,000,000), this is INR 3,600,000 (tooling INR 3,000,000 plus R&D INR 600,000).

Juvoxa Optics, nominated for the Model A headlamp on the strength of our long relationship, has failed crash validation on demo vehicles four consecutive times. This has delayed Model A time-to-market by two months.
Volumes used (quotation file): Year 1 100,000; Year 2 125,000; Year 3 140,000; Year 4 165,000; total 530,000 units.
